name: Tide Hall

text: THE STANDING BOARD. A brass drum, a paper roll and a float in a well,
drawing the height of the harbour as one long shivering line.
It has never once drawn a straight one. That is the point of it.
THE GATE INDICATOR. Three shutters: SEA GATE, RACE, NORTH SLUICE.
Two of them read OPEN. The North Sluice reads SHUT, in red.
A card under it: SHUT SINCE THE SPRING TIDES. TURN IT AND SEE.
A cutaway model of the sea wall, sixteen feet of it in painted tin.
The Hall is the small flooded box in the middle, under the road.
Everything above the flooded box is the city, and the city is drawn very light.
Beside the model, at knee height, a line of small brass studs in the wall.
Each one has a year on it. The highest is above the model's roof.
It is dated the year the Hall was built, which is not a coincidence.
The Hall roll. Two columns: WENT DOWN, and CAME UP DRY.
The second column is empty from top to bottom.
Somebody has ruled it anyway, every year, for forty years.
Eight Bond Crests in a case, one for every Hall in Caelora.
The Tide Crest is third and is the only one with a tide line on it -
a green stain across the lower third, from being kept somewhere honest.
A row of pegs, and on the pegs, thirty coats.
Every one of them is wet. It has not rained in nine days.
The floor under them has a drain cut into it, and the drain is working hard.
A notice, hand-lettered, nailed at the height of a sixteen-year-old:
THE WATER IN HERE IS RUN ON PURPOSE. NOTHING IN HERE IS AN ACCIDENT.
IF IT TAKES YOU, IT MEANT TO. GO WHERE IT PUTS YOU AND LOOK AROUND.

_plan: The gatehouse: the dry room on top of the works, and the Hall's public face in a harbour city of thirty thousand. Everything here is instrumentation -- a tide board, a gate indicator, a cutaway of the sea wall -- because the Tide Hall is not a sports venue with a job attached, it is a flood-defence works that keeps a Hall so somebody walks the gates every day. The stair at 9,2 is the only way down and the only way in; the door at 9,13 is the city's. The gate indicator reading SHUT is the puzzle's brief, posted where the player reads it before they are wet.
